title: Invocation Sankey visualization and proportional alert-smoothing for long-tail token noise
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: Our token-level telemetry surfaced lots of useful per-phase metrics but customers struggle to connect which token phases (prefix, generation, kv-restore, post-processing) are responsible for cost/latency spikes. Separately, alert churn for token-cost SLOs remains high because small invocations with large variance trigger the same thresholds as high-volume endpoints. This PR introduces two complementary observability features: 1) a Sankey-style aggregation (invocation -> token-phase -> cost/latency bucket) to make per-invocation cost flow explorable, and 2) a proportional alert-smoothing algorithm that weights threshold signals by invocation mass to reduce flapping on long-tail noise.

What I changed: single-string summary of changes across repos and services.
- Telemetry ingestion: add token_phase_flow metric (histogram + edges) and sankey_edge_{cost,latency} tags emitted by metrics-service.
- Sampling/enrichment: span-enricher attaches invocation_fingerprint and phase_edge_id for cross-join in tracing.
- Aggregation: metrics-aggregator gains a Sankey rollup job that computes per-interval edge aggregates and stores compact rollups to metrics-store.
- Dashboards: Grafana dashboard "Invocation Sankey & Cost Flow" with interactive edge selection and on-click drilldown to traces.
- Alerts: Prometheus-style rule update introduces alert_mass_weight and Alert Smoothing Controller that applies a rolling-median mass-weighted smoothing window before evaluation (configurable via console flags).
- SDK instrumentation: lightweight helpers in python/ts SDKs to annotate token phases for customers who want richer Sankey edges.

Commits summary: see commits list for details; changes are organized into atomic commits (telemetry, aggregator, dashboard, alerting, SDK).

Testing and rollout: Unit + integration tests added to metrics-service and aggregator. End-to-end validation using replaybench with synthetic workload families (chatty-bursty, short-high-cost, long-low-cost). Canary rollout behind feature flag (observability.sankey.enabled) with gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% across regions. Alert smoothing is off by default and toggled via config during rollout.

Backward/forward compatibility and perf: Metric names and tags are additive; aggregation job uses compact rollups to limit storage. Profiling showed <2% CPU increase on aggregator per 10k rps; batching and pre-aggregation keep index growth bounded.

Related work and tickets: ENG-2372 (design), PM-489 (customer request), SUP-1023 (support case that motivated smoothing), and implementational notes in the PR thread.

release_notes:
- New Grafana dashboard: Invocation Sankey & Cost Flow (interactive per-invocation drilldowns)
- New metrics: token_phase_flow, sankey_edge_cost, sankey_edge_latency
- Alert smoothing controller: proportional, mass-weighted smoothing to reduce alert churn on low-mass invocations
- SDK helpers to annotate token phases for richer observability
Rollout: Feature flag controlled; opt-in canary followed by region ramp.
